record.paper_title: Некоторые экстремальные задачи для векторных расслоений
record.context_brief: Square peg problem for Jordan curves
record.original_question: Does every Jordan curve in the Euclidean plane contain four points that are the vertices of a square inscribed in the curve?

evidence.quote: Неизвестно, во всякую ли жорданову кривую на плоскости можно вписать квадрат.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma:S^1\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be a Jordan curve, i.e., a continuous injective map from the circle into the Euclidean plane, and identify $\gamma$ with its image. Four points $p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4\in\mathbb{R}^2$ are said to be the vertices of an inscribed square in $\gamma$ if they all lie on $\gamma$ and, after suitable ordering, form the vertices of a (non-degenerate) square in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Question: Does every Jordan curve in $\mathbb{R}^2$ contain four points that are the vertices of an inscribed square?
artifact.category_tag: Square peg problem (inscribed squares in Jordan curves)
artifact.status_search_result: The inscribed square problem (Toeplitz's square peg problem) remains open in full generality for arbitrary continuous Jordan curves. It has been resolved for many regularity classes (smooth, piecewise smooth, convex, $C^1$, locally monotone, and, by Greene–Lobb (2020), all smooth Jordan curves with any aspect ratio rectangle), but the general continuous case is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Square peg problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The inscribed square problem... It is an unsolved problem in mathematics whether every Jordan curve admits an inscribed square.
status_evidence.claim: The general case for continuous Jordan curves remains open.

status_evidence.title: Greene-Lobb, 'The rectangular peg problem'
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that every smooth Jordan curve inscribes every rectangle aspect ratio.
status_evidence.claim: Smooth case resolved (including all rectangles), but continuous case still open.
